[[Al-Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] defended the title and claimed their sixth league title after beating [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] in the final. ==Overview== [[Al-Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] defended the championship and claimed their sixth title. The [[Saudi Arabia Football Federation|SAFF]] rules stipulated that both teams in the championship final had to play away, so although both finalists are from [[Riyadh]], the final was played in [[Jeddah]]. Al-Nassr had four coaches during the season. [[Yousef Khamees (footballer, born 1961)|Yousef Khamees]] was the lucky one to win the final, following the successive sackings of [[Jean Fernandez]] and [[Henri Michel]]. ==Clubs== ===Stadia and locations=== {{Location map+ |Saudi Arabia |width=400 |float=right |caption=Locations of teams in the 1994-95 Saudi Premier League |places= {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=21.54333 |long=39.17278 |label=[[Jeddah]] |position=left}} {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=24.68800|long=46.72243 |label=[[Riyadh]] |position=left}} {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=26.40000|long=50.15000 |label=[[Dammam]] |position=right}} {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=26.28333|long=50.20000 |label=[[Khobar]] }} {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=21.41667|long=39.81667 |label=[[Mecca]] }} {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=26.084|long=43.994 |label=[[Unaizah]]|position=right}} {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=26.33333|long=43.96667 |label=[[Buraidah]] |position=left}} }} {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !
